LAW OF PORTS FOR THE ISLAND OF CUBA.
————
CHAPTER I.
OWNERSHIP OF COAST WATERS, OF THE SHORES OF THE
SEA, ACCRETIONS AND EASEMENTS OF ADJOINING LANDS.
ARTICLE 1. The following are national property and
for public use, without prejudice to the rights of
individuals:
First. The littoral zone, which is that portion of the
coast or sea limits of the Spanish territory which lies
between ebb and flow, where tides are perceptible, or
which is covered by the highest surfs during storms,
where they are not.
Said littoral zone extends also along the banks of
rivers as far as they are navigable or tides are
perceptible.
Second. The coast waters or maritime zone which
girt the coasts of Spanish domain, throughout the
width determined by international law, with their
coves, roadsteads, bays, harbors and other havens
available for fishing and navigation Within said zone
the State is in charge of the surveillance and utilities,
as also of the right of asylum and immunity, in
accordance to law and international treaties.
ART. 2. The lands that are added to the littoral
zone through accretions and deposits caused by the
sea are of public ownership. When by reason of said
accretions and owing to the withdrawal of the sea the
interior line limiting the said zone advances toward
the former, the surplus lands remaining from the
former littoral zone shall become the property of the
State, after the proper survey thereof by the department of the colonies, with the approval of that of the

426

navy; and the former may alienate them when they
are not considered necessary for maritime or other
services of public utility. Should they be alienated in
accordance to law, the right of refusal shall be
granted to the owners of the adjoining lands.
ART. 3. Islands already formed, or which may be
formed, within the littoral zone and in estuaries and
mouths of rivers that are considered maritime harbors, under this law, are the property of the State. But
if such islands should be created by the cutting of a
river through lands of private ownership they shall
continue to belong to the owner of the dismembered
estate or estates, reserving the rights which private
individuals may have.
ART. 4. Anchorages, ship-ya rds, docks, arsenals, and
other establishments intended by the Government for
the exclusive use of the navy, are the property of the
State. First and second class harbors of general
interest are national property and for public use.
ART. 5. Everything cast upon the shore by the sea
and which has no known owner belongs to the State.
‘The treasury department, after the proper inventory
and appraisal, shall seize it, and shall be liable for
the claims of a third person and for the payment of
charges and rewards for the finding and salvage
thereof, in accordance with the prescriptions of laws
and regulations.
ART. 6. The Government, without prejudice to the
obligations and rights of the owners and consignees,
shall provide for the salvage of wrecked vessels, their
cargoes and effects, and also  for their recovery from
the wreck in case of a total loss, in accordance with
the provisions of maritime ordinances and regulations.

427

Consular agents shall exercise the proper intervention according to international agreements with
regard to the nations they represent.
ART. 7. Private lands adjoining the sea or lying
within the littoral zone are subject to the easements
of salvage and coast surveillance.
ART. 8. The salvage ease ment has the same
extension on private lands adjoining the sea as on the
littoral zone within which they are situated and 20
meters in addition thereto toward the interior of the
lands; and public use shall be made thereof for the
purpose of saving and deposi ting the flotsam, effects,
and cargoes of wrecked vessels.
Fishing vessels may also beach within this zone of
easement when compelled to do so on account of the
condition of the sea, and in the same manner deposit
their effects on land while the storm rages.
This zone of easement shall advance or recede with
the advance or recession of the sea, as established in
general for the littoral zone.
For damages caused to prope rty on the occasion of
a salvage an indemnity shall be proper, but only to
the extent of the value of the objects saved, after the
expenses of assistance given and rewards to finders
have been paid according to law.
ART. 9. The salvage easement is not an obstacle to
owners of lands adjoining the sea from sowing and
planting on their premises within the littoral zone
and constructing agricultural buildings and country
resorts thereon.
In order to build in such places, notice must first be
given to the governor of the province, who, after
hearing the naval commander and the chief engineer

428

of public works, may withhold his consent should it
cause any obstruction to the exercise of the easement
referred to in the foregoing article.
ART. 10. The coast surveillance easement consists
of the obligation to leave free a general passage 6
meters wide adjoining the highest water line or that
reached by the surf during the heaviest storms where
tides are not perceptible, to be established when
necessary by the governor-general of the island after
hearing the naval authorities . In places where it is
difficult or dangerous to pass, the passage may be
carried more than 6 meters inland, but without
exceeding what, in the opinion of said authority, is
strictly necessary.
The surveillance easement, in extraordinary cases
and when necessary for the service of the State, is
imposed alike on lands that are fenced in, as on those
that are open. Property which has not been subject to
the surveillance easement until the promulgation of
the water law of August 3, 1886, and subsequently
thereto has suffered visible and material damages
through the imposition of said easement, shall be
paid the proper indemnity for said damage.
CHAPTER II.
USE AND UTILIZATION OF THE
COAST WATERS AND BEACHES.
ART. 11. Only the owners of ponds, lakes, or basins
of sea water in private property, having no navigable
communication with the sea, have a right to fish
therein without any restrictions but those relating to
public health.
ART. 12. The free use of the coast waters, coves,
roadsteads, bays, and haven s is understood for the

429

purposes of navigation, fishing, shipping and landing,
anchoring, and other simila r acts, within the legal
prescriptions and police regulations relating thereto.
The same is the case with regard to the public use of
beaches, which under similar restrictions is granted
to everybody for traveling, bathing, spreading and
drying clothes, casting nets, beaching, careening and
building ships, bathing cattle, picking shells, plants,
and shellfish.
CHAPTER III.
CLASSIFICATION OF PORTS.
ART. 13. For the purposes of this law ports are
those places on the coast more or less protected,
either by reason of the natural lay of the land or by
expressly constructed works, and wherein maritime
traffic is carried on in a permanent and legal manner.
ART. 14. Estuaries and mouths of rivers are
likewise considered as ports up to where the tides are
perceptible, and where there are none, up to where
the surf reaches during ordinary storms, altering
their usual flow, Above these points the banks or
margins of rivers pre-ser ve their special fluvial
character.
ART. 15. Ports are classified as first and second
class ports of general interest, and ports of local or
provincial and municipal interest.
Ports of general interest are considered those
specially destined to ancho ring grounds, mercantile
depots, loading and unloading of vessels employed in
maritime trade, when such trade may be of interest
to several provinces, and when said ports are in
direct communication with the principal centers of
production of the island of  the Peninsula, and of

430

foreign countries. Ports of re fuge, so called owing to
their position and special advantages of capacity,
security, and shelter during storms, are also of
general interest.
Ports of local interest, or provincial and municipal
ports, are those principally destined for anchoring
grounds, loading and unloading of vessels employed
in local industry and commerce, without prejudice to
being classified among those of general interest when
their trade may extend to other localities, territories,
or provinces.
The foregoing classification can not be altered
except by virtue of a law.
ART. 16. Ports of the island  which are qualified for
foreign trade or commerce on the high seas are
declared first-class ports of general interest.
Ports not so qualified, at which coasting vessels
engaged between two or more provinces make a stop,
are declared second-class ports of general interest.
ART. 17. All ports not included in the preceding
article, and in which commercial trade is carried on;
are declared ports of local interest.
CHAPTER IV.
EXECUTION AND MAINTENANCE OF WORKS IN PORTS,
THEIR MANAGEMENT AND POLICE.
ART. 18. It shall be the duty of the colonial
secretary to order the survey and preparation of
plans for all kinds of works in ports of general
interest; to approve the same and order their execution after hearing the department of the navy; to
grant concessions, make service regulations, designate the necessary personnel, and prescribe the

431

duties of officials depending on the department of the
colonies who are to direct and supervise the works.
ART. 19. In harbor works in ports of provincial
interest the same duties devolve upon the provincial
deputation as are assigned to the department of the
colonies in the preceding article, except where the
works should affect lands of public ownership. in
which case the provisions of Chapter VIII of the
general law of public works must be observed.
Similar duties appertain to municipal councils with
regard to municipal harbors.
The plans for works in ports corresponding to the
provincial deputation or municipal councils shall,
after the proper naval authorities have passed
thereon, be submitted for the approval of the colonial
department, which is also intrusted with the
technical direction of the works and the appointment
of the personnel required thereon.
ART. 20. The same duties appertain to the navy
department, with regard to the surveys, plans, and
execution of works in ports having military arsenals,
in so far as they relate to the latter ports.
ART. 21. The establishment, repair, maintenance,
and cleaning of ports, and management, service, and
police thereof, in all civil matters appertain, in ports
of general interest, to the colonial department, and in
ports of local interest, to the deputations or municipal
councils, according as to whether they are of a
provincial or municipal character.
ART. 22. The port service is divided into two
classes, one relating to the general shipping traffic,
arrivals, departures, anchorages, berths, moorings
and unmoorings at wharves; towing and maritime
assistance appertain to the naval authority; and the

432

other, including the execution and maintenance of
the works and buildings, operations of loading and
unloading on wharves, traffic on the same and within
its zone of service, and all that relates to the use of
the various works, intended for the trade of the port,
which appertain to the colonial department.
ART 23. The governor-general of the island, as the
superior chief of all the branches of the civil
administration and as delegate of the colonial department, is the chief of all such  services at the ports as
are in charge of said colonial department.
ART. 24. Subject to the general service regulations
and to the orders and instructions of the colonial
department, and under the authority of the governorgeneral of the island, the engineers of roads, canals,
and ports shall have charge of the survey and
direction of all the work s and supervision of the
services comprised in the second class mentioned in
article 22, excepting such works and services as
pertain to the military arsenals.
ART. 25. Port of general interest shall be
maintained by the State, according to the sums
appropriated therefor in the general budgets and
those included in their respective budgets by the
deputations and municipal councils when these
corporations wish to contribute toward the expenses
of said ports. The works shall be executed either by
officials of the administrat ion or by contract, as may
be determined in each case.
ART. 26. The Government may provide for the cost
of harbor works by means of  special taxes levied in
the locality, to be exclusively applied to said works,
independently of the general State budget, and
organize boards of harbor  works intrusted with the

433

administration and disbur sement of funds and the
execution of the works, under the supervision and
surveillance of the colonial department.
ART. 27. The colonial department shall issue
general regulations for the organization and management of existing boards of harbor works and for such
as may hereafter be established. The appointment
and removal of the chief engi neer of said works shall
he subject to the will of the Government, which may
also appoint special delegates on the said boards
whenever it may consider it advisable.
ART. 28. Works in ports of general interest,
including such as have been planned or begun for the
account of the State, may al so be executed by means
of concessions to private companies, in accordance
with the general law of public works.
ART. 29. Ports of local interest shall be maintained
with funds of the deputations or municipal councils,
according as to whether the works are provincial or
municipal. Toward the execution of works in ports
pertaining to deputations, the State and municipal
councils may contribute, either by furnishing skilled
officials or. by making appropriations for the purpose
in their respective budgets. In like manner the State
and provincial deputations may contribute toward
harbor works which may be instituted by municipalities.
The surveys and plans and their approval as well
as the concessions of provincial and municipal harbor
works shall be made in accordance with the provisions of articles 39 and 48 of the general law of
public works.
ART. 30. The proper instructions for the formation
and approval of plans of new works in harbors,

434

stating the formalities and reports which must
precede said approval, shall be included in the
regulations for the execution of said law.
ART. 31. At every port there shall be a littoral zone
of service, to be fixed by the colonial department, in
each case, for the operation of loading and unloading,
warehousing and transportation of goods, and the
transit of persons and vehicles. The approval and
project of said zone, and the apportionment thereof
for the different services, carry with them the
declaration of public utility, and such private lands or
buildings as lie within it are subject to the exercise of
the right of eminent domain.
ART. 32. The governor of the province, after hearing
the captain of the port, the chief engineer, the
provincial board of health, and the collector of customs, shall mark out and assign the zones of the port
to the different services on the wharves, and shall
decide all questions that may arise with regard to
their use and police, when th e port in question is of
local interest; if it be of general interest, the
governor-general of the island shall have these
duties. From the decisions an appeal lies to the
governor-general or to th e secretary of the colonies,
as the case may be.
ART. 33. Whenever a vessel is wrecked within a
port her owners, or the consignees of the insurance
companies shall proceed to raise her within the term
fixed by the naval commander of the province. Should
they not do so, the secretary of the navy shall order it
done, deducting the cost from the proceeds of the
vessel and goods which it may contain.
ART. 34. If, either willfully or through carelessness,
any damage should be caused by vessels or their

435

mooring cables to the works of any port, or the latter
should thereby be fouled, the captain of the port shall
cause the parties responsible therefor to pay, in
addition to the fines in stamped paper established by
the regulations, the sum at  which the engineer may
estimate the necessary repairs, the latter amount to.
be paid into the Treasury.
ART. 35. Besides the general regulations for the
execution of this law, special-service and police bylaws shall be framed for ea ch port, containing the
provisions relating to its use, and which must he
approved by the colonial department, procuring the
greatest uniformity in these regulations, in so far as
possible, through the different conditions of each port
for the benefit of commerce and maritime industry.
CHAPTER V.
SERVICES CONNECTED WITH PORTS.
ART. 36. The pilot service in ports of the Spanish
domain shall continue to be in charge of the navy
department.
ART. 37. Lights and beacons, being services
connected with that of the po rts, shall continue to be
in charge of the colonial department. The maritime
watch stations and semaphores and lifeboats shall be
in charge of the same, but shall depend immediately
on the superior naval authority of the island.
CHAPTER VI.
WORKS EXECUTED BY PRIVATE PERSONS.
ART. 38. At no points on the coasts, beaches, ports,
and mouths of rivers, or on the islands formed within
the littoral zone, can new works of any kind be
executed, or buildings constructed without the proper

436

authorization, in accordance with the provisions of
this law.
ART. 39. Permission to build temporary barracks or
constructions designed for bat hs shall be granted by
the governors, in maritime capitals, and in other
towns, by the mayors, after consulting the naval
authority, if said constructions are to be built outside
the port; but if within the same the chief engineer
shall also be heard, in addition to the naval
authority.
ART. 40. Permission to establish other services or
improvements of a temporary character within the
littoral zone, which is national property and for
public use, shall be granted by the naval commanders
of the provinces, provided they do not interfere with
tie common uses to which sa id zone is devoted, and
after hearing the governors and chief engineers of
public works, where such concessions might affect
other services under the control of the colonial office
or some other branch of the administration.
ART. 41. Such permissions shall be revoked
whenever necessary for a proper surveillance and
service of the coasts, the town and rural police, or the
concession of the land for other purposes of greater
utility and importance, afte r instituting an inquiry
and hearing the person interested before the
authority who may have granted the permission.
In such cases the owners of the temporary
constructions shall dispose only of the materials employed without any right to indemnity.
ART. 42. When the constructions and improvements
referred to in the foregoing articles are of a permanent character, the autho rization shall be granted

437

by the secretary of the colonies, after hearing the
secretary of the navy.
ART. 43. Works for coast defense to protect private
estates or buildings against the beating of the waves,
even though of a permane nt character, shall be
authorized by the governor of the province, after
hearing the opinion of the naval authorities and of
the chief engineer of public works.
ART. 44. It is the duty of the colonial secretary to
grant authorization, after hearing the naval authorities, for the construction on the sea or beaches and
adjoining lands, or in ports, whether for private or
public use, of such w harves, quays, dockyards,
floating docks, shipyards, and other similar works as
are complementary and auxiliary to those existing for
the service of the port. Such authorization shall not
constitute a monopoly, and therefore others may be
granted for the same clas s of works in the same
harbor, beach, or stretch of  coast, provided the public
service or use does not suffer thereby.
ART. 45. It is the duty of the colonial secretary,
after hearing the naval authorities, to grant authorization for the establishmen t of salt ponds, works,
and other buildings which may wholly or in part
occupy public lands for private use.
ART. 46. It is the duty of the secretary of the navy
to grant concessions for a ll sorts of fisheries, fish
garths, crawls, shellfish nurseries, in accordance with
the ordinances and regulations in force thereon or
that may hereafter be established.
ART. 47. The colonial department may authorize
private individuals or companies, under the terms
prescribed in the general law of public works, to
construct ports at places on the coast where there are

438

no works or plans of other ports that are classified, or
where no special rights  exist for the use and
utilization of said place, after hearing the navy department.
ART. 48. When’ the works of a port the concession
of which is applied for, whether in conformity with
the plan of the applicant, or subject to the one
surveyed and approved by the colonial department,
refers to one in which, although no work has yet been
executed, there exists a leg ally authorized maritime
commerce, and services are performed with more or
less perfection, the concession must be granted under
such conditions as may be necessary to reserve in.
full force the existing rights of entering the port,
anchoring, loading, and unloading, afloat or on the
coast, so that none of th e services that are freely
exercised or enjoyed by the public may be made
compulsory.
ART. 49. Proper authorization may also be granted
to a private company for executing the works of a
port in charge of the State or for completing those
which are constructed or suspended, or carrying out
one part of the plan wh ile the State executes the
other, in which case special conditions may be
established in compensation of the expenses thereof
and for the benefit of the company in the shape of the
cession of the land where the works are carried on,
for a limited time, or other privileges, according to
the available portion of the work, the cost of those
that may be executed and the nature or importance of
the public services existing in the port, provided prior
rights to the use of the port and its works are
reserved in full force, as stated in the preceding
article.

439

ART. 50. In case works declar ed of public utility are
to be executed in a port by the State, the deputations,
or municipal councils, and in order to carry them out
it should become necessary to utilize or destroy those
constructed by private persons by virtue of concessions granted them, the concessionaries shall have a
right to be indemnified only for the value of the
material employed in said works, after an appraisement by experts made in conformity with the general
regulations for the execution of this law.
ART. 51. The colonial department shall grant
authorization for draining, cultivating, or otherwise
improving salt marshes belonging to the State, or of
public ownership, and such as do not belong to town
commons or other property devoted to general use.
In order to request of the colonial department a
declaration of lands pertaining to town commons, or
devoted to general use, a period of one year is allowed
from the date of the public ation of this law. If the
towns fail to obtain a favor able decision or the term
expires without an application having been made for
such declaration, said salt marshes shall be considered as waste lands; this, ho wever, not to interfere in
any case with the free public use of their natural
products.
Salt marshes of private ownership may be drained
by their owners with the consent of the governor, who
shall give it after hearing the naval authority and the
chief engineer of the province, provided navigation
and fishing are not injured thereby.
For the draining and improvement of salt marshes
that may be declared unhealthy, the provisions
contained in the water law regarding marsh lands
shall be observed.

440

ART. 52. The concessions referred to in the foregoing articles shall be subject to the formalities
mentioned in the general regulations for the execution of this law.
ART. 53. Authorization for the survey or for
drawing the plans of the works included in articles 44
and 45, and those mentioned  in articles 47 and 51,
shall be granted by the Governor-General of the
island after receiving the report of the general
inspector of public works of the same.
Those comprised in article 46 shall be granted by
the naval commander of the maritime, province to
which they belong.
ART. 54. The concessions of works and public lands
mentioned in articles 44, 45, 47, and 48 shall be
granted by the colonial department without any
public bid or limited term, subject to the provisions of
article 50. Should there be more than one application
for the same or similar wo rk, or the plans presented
prove incompatible owing to their occupying a portion
of public property used in common on the beaches,
shores, or ports, where th ey may be established,
those plans shall he preferred which offer the
greatest advantages, and if they be equal, the one
first presented.
ART. 55. Concessions of salt marshes shall be
granted without public bids and in perpetuity, except
in case some private party or company should
demand an award by bids, presenting to that effect a
proposition in which a stand ard of valuation is fixed
and offered, guaranteed by a temporary deposit equal
to said standard, which shall serve as a basis for the
bid. If the person obtaining the award should not be
the author of the plan approved for the drainage

441

works, he shall have to pay the cost of said plan to
the author, appraised in accordance with the
provisions governing such cases in bids for public
works, or in the manner prescribed by the regulations.
ART. 56. Concessions of works in the cases referred
to in article 49 shall be granted through bids and for
a limited period. The bids shall be made upon any
one of these three bases, namely:
The appraisal of the existing works and of the
constructions and lands to be utilized; the reduction
of the tariff rates charged for the use of the works;
the period of time during which the company is to
enjoy the benefits of the works.
The colonial department shall fix the basis,
standard, and conditions for the bid, taking into
consideration the plans and proposals that may have
been presented requesting the concession.
ART. 57. In concessions of works in ports, whereby
lands are reclaimed from th e sea, there shall always
be excepted, out of the lands recognized as the property of the concessioner, that portion which may be
necessary for the service zone referred to in article
31, which shall remain the property of the State.
ART. 58. In every concession of public or private
works there shall be fixed:
First. The period for which the concession is granted.
Second. The terms within which the works are to
be begun and concluded.
Third. The proportional part of the estimate which
has to be spent in each of the periods that it may be
thought advisable to fix in order to carry out the

442

concession within the full term allowed for the termination of the works.
Fourth. The conditions for the establishment and
use of the work as may be necessary in order not to
injure acquired rights and general interests.
Fifth. The bond required of the concessioner in the
case of a public work, to guarantee the execution
thereof; and,
Sixth. The case where the concession may be declared forfeited, as well as the consequences thereof.
ART. 59. When a declaration of public utility is
requested by private persons in behalf of any work,
the procedure prescribed by the general law of public
works for said declaration shall be observed.
ART. 60. He who shall have enjoyed during twenty
years the usufruct of some maritime industry established on public property without opposition on the
part of the authority or of a third party, shall
continue to enjoy the same, even though he fail to
show that he had obtained proper authority therefor;
this right shall be understood  as in force so long as
the class ‘of industry or the application of the space
occupied have undergone no changes or alterations
during the aforesaid twenty  years; and otherwise it
shall be declared forfeited unless authorization be
obtained as in the case of a new work, and in the
manner prescribed in this law.
ART. 61. All laws, royal de crees, regulations, royal
orders, and other provisions conflicting with this law
are hereby repealed.
ART. 62. The governor-general of the island may
anticipate the concessions of  the works included in
this chapter, and which, according to the provisions

443

thereof, it is the duty of  the colonial department to
grant, without prejudice to, and reserving the definite decision which may be proper if the persons
interested accept this condition, and provided there is
no opposition or objection  on the part of the corporations or officials interested, being obliged otherwise to forward to the colonial department the
respective proceedings with their report for a final
decision.
Approved by Royal Decree of this date.
FABIÉ
Madrid, October 31, 1890.
(Gaceta of December 13.)

OFFICIAL GAZETTE
MINISTRY OF PUBLIC WORKS
Decree No. 467.
After re-examination of the file submitted to the
Civil Government of La Habana Province arising from
the request and project submitted by Mr. Sylvester
Scovel in connection with an administrative concession for the construction of a jetty/dock with
mechanical installations, a building for Customs
Offices, a special Department for Customs Inspectors,
apparatus for loading and unloading, and other
accessory works at the port of this Capital.
Whereas, in a Decree issued by this Office of the
President dated last February 27, these works were
declared to be of public utility, ordering the holding of
an auction for the concession necessary to execute said
works on the basis of the petitioner’s project after
valuation of said project and pertinent announcements.
Whereas verification of said valuation revealed a
project value of fifty-nine thousand five hundred fortyseven pesos, forty-five cents ($59,547.45) Cy. and the
conditions under which the concession should be
granted were defined, the petitioner declaring his
acceptance of said valuation and conditions.
Whereas the auction ceremony was scheduled for
the ninth day of this month of November at two p.m.
at this Ministry, which was announced in the
OFFICIAL GAZETTE and the “Diario de la Marina,”
“Discusion,”and “Mundo” newspapers of this City in
five consecutive issues, repeated in the first ten of the
months of this past July, August, September, and
October, as well as in those of Paris, “Le Figaro,” “Le
Matin,” “Le Temps,” and “Le Journal;” in “Track

445
Kischer Kurier” of Berlin, and in London and New
York, where printed copies of the project were sent and
made available to the public, including a copy of
related drawings.
Whereas, with the Board with jurisdiction to hear
the auction was in session on the scheduled day, time
and place, with the assist ance of a Civil Law Notary,
the pertinent instrument was drawn up; of the three
proposals submitted, the one submitted by Mr. D.
Aceituno, which offered a twenty-seven percent (27%)
reduction on the rates submitted by the project
planner and reduced to fifty (50) years the ninety-nine
(99) requested by the la tter since the works were
limited, was declared to be the most advantageous, the
proposal of the petitioner, who insisted on the entirety
of his project in said regard, and the other proposal,
which, though it reduced to nine (9) years the term of
the concession, only made a six percent (6%) reduction
to the rates.
Whereas the legitimate representative of Compañía
del Puerto [Port Company], successor of Mr. Scovel,
creator of the project, in ex ercise of its right of preemption at the auction ceremony and within the legal
timeframe, accepted Mr. Aceituno’s proposal on behalf
of the Company they represent.
Whereas this file meets all requirements and
complies with all formalities required by Law for the
granting of the concession in question.
Whereas, pursuant to the Regulation for enforcement of the General Public Works Law, the approved
project must serve as the basis for the auction and the
proposals must first address the reductions of rates for
use of the work, and according to Article 8 of the
Technical Regulation, for the processing of concessions

446
to private individuals for port works on this Island, the
auction must also be based firstly on the reduction of
rates, followed by the term of the concession.
Whereas, in this regard, the declaration of the Board
overseeing the auction to the effect that Mr. D.
Aceituno’s proposal is the most advantageous is legal
and proper since it complies with the abovementioned
current legal provisions, as it is the one that reduced
the rates to the lowest extent.
Whereas Compañía del Puerto, as Mr. Scovel’s
successor, having availed itself in a timely and legal
manner of the right of pre- emption conferred upon it
by Article 38 of the Regulation of the Public Works
Law, it fully subrogated Mr. Aceituno, whose proposal
it accepted, wherefore it is proper to consider it the
winner of the auction and award it the concession.
Pursuant to the abovementioned provisions and
those contained in the General Public Works Law and
the Regulation for its enforcement, and in the Ports
Law and its Technical Regulation, and in the Law of
September 11, 1879 on auctions for works and
services.
Based on the proposal made by the Minister of
Public Works, and by the authority vested in me, I
award Compañía del Puerto, successor of Mr. Sylvester
Scovel, the concession necessary to execute the works
contained in the project submitted by Mr. Scovel on
August 22, 1904, subject to the following conditions:
1.- The works will comply with the project submitted
by the petitioner, Mr. Sylvester Scovel, dated August
22, 1904, in all respects not subsequently modified in
the following clauses.

447
2.- This concession is understood as included among
those defined in Articles 44 and 45 of the Ports Law of
October 31, 1890 and Article 97 of the General Public
Works Law of April 19, 1883, and is granted for a term
of fifty (50) years starting on the date of the concession,
subject to the provisions of Article 50 of the
abovementioned Ports Law.
3.- Authorization is given for the establishment of
the coal deposit and its operation on the south side of
the jetty as outlined in the project, subject to the
concessionaire having the obligation to take any
measures needed to prevent dust from this coal from
getting inside the buildings of the Customs Offices, the
buildings of this city, or from becoming a nuisance to
the public.
4.- The State gives in usufruct during the term of the
concession the section of the San Francisco docks, as
well as the area of public domain that will be occupied
by the project works.
5.- As compensation and in payment for occupation
of this section, as well as the impairment of general
use caused by execution of the works, the
concessionaire undertakes to:
(a) Transfer the building for the Customs Inspectors’
Department that is part of the project to the State free
of charge.
(b) Widen the entrance street  to the jetty to thirtysix (36) feet, as indicated in the project drawings.
(c) Build a twenty-four (24) foot wide street on the
jetty that is paved in the same fashion as other streets
in the project that will run from North to South along
said jetty, separating it from the Customs Agents

448
Department; the roof over this street will be at least
fifteen (15) feet high.
(d) Install a scale at the entrance to the Customs
Inspectors’ Department in a location specified by the
Port Customs Authority, the manufacturer of which
will be specified by said Authority, to be used to weigh
any items transferred to said Department by either
the concessionaire’s equipment or by carts from the
public docks.
(e) Permanently transfer to the State at no cost all
expansion work done on the Passenger Ticket Office
intended for the Custom s Offices, subject to the
condition that this building may not be used for any
purpose other than said Offices.
(f) Set aside for public use the dock on the north side
of the projected jetty, subject to the condition that at
any time during the concession, when it believes port
traffic makes it necessary, the concessionaire may
install equipment and machinery on said north side
for the loading and unloading of vessels and
steamships, enlarging the building for this purpose,
ensuring its suitability for the plant that was
improved. It may exercise this right by providing two
months’ advance notice to the Ministry of Public
Works, submitting the relevant drawings therewith,
whereafter the additional works will be included in the
concession.
6.- In the event that, purs uant to the provisions of
Article 50 of the Ports Law, it becomes necessary to
expropriate the works, the concessionaire will be
entitled to remove from the dock/jetty any machinery,
material, rolling stock, equipment, or devices in use at
such a time.

449
7.- If, at any time during the term of the concession,
the works are expropriated, also pursuant to Article 50
of the Ports Law mentioned above, the Government or
its agencies will compensate the concessionaire for the
value of all works constructed by it, including the
Customs Inspectors’ Department and the dock on the
north side of the jetty, but not for the value of the
machinery, rolling stock, equipment, and devices
referred to in the preceding clause in the event the
concessionaire decides to remove them.
8.- In the event of the ex propriation referred to in
the two preceding clauses, the works will be appraised
by direct measurement of th eir volume, applying the
prices set for the units of works contained in the
budget subject to the requirements provided in
Paragraph 2 of Article 14 of the Technical Regulation
for the Ports Law of November 17, 1890.
9.- The State will allow the concessionaire to freely
use a large space on the site of the works, including
access thereto, for storage and handling of tools and
materials, and for any oper ations in connection with
construction of the works.
10.- During the term of the concession, it will be the
concessionaire’s responsibility to maintain the
foundations, streets, buildings, machinery, and other
installations of the plant in good condition to ensure it
turns the works over to the Government in perfect
working order at the end of said term. The
Government will be responsible for any repairs and
renovations that need to be verified at the building set
aside for the Customs Offices , and the section of the
dock/jetty set aside for the public on the north side, as
well as maintenance of the pavement on the seafront
service area along the entire front side of the jetty with
the land side.

450
11.- The concessionaire will not be liable for any
damages resulting from delays on its part in
construction of the plant at the project when such
delay was caused by strike, shipwreck, cyclones,
epidemics, or any other force majeure events.
12.- During the term of the concession, the
concessionaire may add to the project plant’s
machinery, devices, and equipment anything it deems
necessary to ensure proper management of the traffic
at said plant, and may also make any improvements
to said machinery, devices, and equipment that may be
advantageous from time to time.
13.- The concessionaire will install machines needed
for the generation of electricity, using steam engines,
though it is entitled to acquire electrical power by
agreement with any Companies able to supply it, in
which case it will not be  obligated to make these
installations or use them if they were already made.
14.- The concessionaire may choose the means of
implementation, agents, and other employees for the
construction, maintenance, and Administration of the
works.
15.- The concessionaire may freely use the elevated
rail that runs through the Customs Inspectors’
Department, as well as the right to enter and exit said
building, to carry out any repair and maintenance
work it deems necessary for the purposes of the
concession.
16.- During the term of the concession, neither the
section of the dock/jetty on the north side that is
intended for the public, or the Customs Inspectors’
Department, may be set aside for any use other than
those assigned to them in this project. The State will
not permit the provision of mechanical services such

451
as those used by the concessionaire for its operations
on said part of the jetty.
17.- The concessionaire permanently transfers to
the State all expansion work on the Passenger Ticket
Office intended for the Customs Offices, subject to the
condition that this building may not be used for any
purpose other than the establishment of said Offices.
18.- In the event the State ceases using the works
referred to in the two preceding clauses, the
Government will hand over the dock and Customs
Inspectors’ Department to the concessionaire for its
use and operation during the term of the concession,
but will retain ownership of the expansion works for
the Customs Offices building, compensating the
concessionaire for their value based on an appraisal to
be conducted at such a time and in line with their
condition at said time, wh ereafter the Government
may set aside said building for any use it deems
appropriate.
19.- The works comprisi ng the project are
concessioned for public se rvice, subject to the rates
accepted in the auction for them, whose applicable
bases and rules are contained in the project
documents, and a rate higher than the one authorized
cannot be demanded; said rate must be displayed to
the public in a visible location.
20.- The application of these rates will be subject to
the regulation attached thereto, though only to the
extent their rules are not contrary to Customs
Regulations and Ordinances and any other applicable
related provisions, or any of a general nature that may
be henceforth enacted.
21.- After receiving a complaint from the concessionaire, employees tasked wi th the maintenance and

452
policing of State docks will take appropriate action in
line with the provisions of Article 26 of the Regulation
for the Maintenance and Policing of State Docks
against any consignees of boats and merchandise who
allow refuse from broken flat tiles, tiles, bricks, etc., or
straw, cane, and other materials used for the stowage
of vessels to be thrown on the jetty in violation of
Article 4 of said Regulation.
22.- Government vessels and those carrying goods
intended for use by the State and its different sectors
will enjoy preference when it comes to mooring,
loading, and unloading on the jetty, provided the Head
of the Office in question so requests, paying half of the
rate established for other vessels for this service.
23.- The concessionaire is barred from granting any
other preference for use of the jetty and its equipment,
with the exception of the condition mentioned above,
which will be according to the priority of the request,
for which it will keep a chronological register of all
requests it receives that it  must show to anyone so
requesting.
24.- Any regulations issued by the concessionaire for
operations on the jetty will be in complete harmony
with current Customs Regulations and Ordinances or
any enacted henceforth, as well as the inspection and
actions of Customs Authorities.
25.- Before commencing wo rks, the Chief Engineer
of the District, with the assistance of the
concessionaire, will carry out the setting out of the
works to be executed in accordance with the project, a
record of which will be issued in triplicate, one copy of
which will be submitted with the pertinent drawing for
approval of the Ministry of Public Works, and once this
is obtained, the other copy will be provided to the

453
concessionaire, and the third copy will be archived at
the District Public Works Office.
26.- The concessionaire will commence work within
four (4) months from the date of the concession and
will execute them in the following order and term:
1.- The new Customs Offices must without fail be
ready for occupation in three months.
2.- The Customs Inspectors’ Department in the steel
and cement building with its electrical mechanism for
the handling of parcels, everything ready for use in
thirteen months.
3.- The sidings and the five transverse sections
south of the cement and steel building, which include
a portion of the same, measuring six hundred forty
(640) feet in length from Ea st to West by eighty (80)
feet in width from north to south, with an installation
of “Locohoist” fixed tracks ready for use in twenty-two
(22) months.
4.- The next seven transverse sections from the
building with all related equipment ready for use in
twenty-eight (28) months.
5.- The remaining fill dirt for the building and public
dock in forty (40) months.
6.- In order for operation of all sections of the
projected plant to be underway at the end of the forty
(40) month term.
27.- All terms mentioned in the preceding article are
understood to start on the date of the concession.
28.- Inspection of execution of the works, as well as
compliance with these conditions, will be the
responsibility of the Chief Engineer of Public Works in
the District.

454
29.- Upon completion of the works, the Chief
Engineer will carefully insp ect them, and if it is
determined that all provisions of this concession have
been complied with during the execution, and that said
works are in perfect working order, he will make this
a matter of record in a certificate to be issued in
triplicate, one of which will be sent to the Ministry of
Public Works for its approval, and, once this is
obtained, the others will be distributed as indicated for
the setting out record.
30.- All expenses arising from the setting out,
inspection, and acceptance of the works will be borne
by the concessionaire, including expenses for
inspection in foreign factories of the steel intended for
use in the buildings and machinery, to which end the
concessionaire will deposit one thousand pesos
($1,000.00) a month at a place indicated to it during
the entire duration of the inspection of the factories to
bear its expense.
31.- This concession is understood to be made
without prejudice to third parties, except for the right
to property and with the understanding that the
concessionaire will be bound by as many provisions of
a general nature that have been enacted or that are
hereafter enacted with regard to these kinds of
concessions.
32.- This concession will expire if the concessionaire
fails to comply with any of these provisions binding it,
the consequences of said expiration being those
provided by the General Public Works Law and its
Regulation.
33.- Upon expiration of the term of the concession,
the State will replace the concessionaire in possession
of the works and will immediately come into

455
enjoyment of it and its proc eeds, together with all its
machinery, rolling stock, equipment, devices, and any
improvements made thereto. The concessionaire will
have the obligation to turn  over the works and its
operating material in good condition and working
order.
In the five years prior to the end of the concession,
the Government will be entitled to withhold the liquid
proceeds from the works, and to use them to keep them
in good condition, in the event the concessionaire does
not attempt to fully carry out this obligation.
Havana, November 29, 1905.
T. ESTRADA PALMA,
President.
Rafael Montalvo,
Minister of Public Works

PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT
DECREE No. 1944
Whereas: Port of Havana Docks Company, in a
pleading dated October 15,  1919, addressed to the
Secretary of Public Works, represents that: under the
terms of Decree number 1022 of November 11, 1910,
it is obliged to build dock “C” ten years after the
termination of dock “B,” and dock “D” five years after
the termination of dock “C”; and that for the purpose
of improving existing conditions it would immediately
undertake the construction of the rest of the works,
provided that the State, on its part, would agree to
certain modifications that would redound to the
benefit of the public service it provides.
Whereas: Said modifications consist, first, in
consolidating into one single body the constructions
corresponding to docks “C” and “D” on the site indicated on the attached plan for dock “C,” thereby
significantly increasing the effective area of the
consolidated dock or jetty and achieving greater
capacity for the handling of merchandise; second,
expanding the existing docks “A” and “B” by building
two 9.15 m.-wide side strips, as shown on the plan.
And third, building on the side strips projected for
the three jetties double railroad tracks that will
connect to another double railroad track which is to
be laid down on the spac e between the building on
the edge and the fence fronting the street, which, in
turn, will connect to the existing parallel tracks in
front of the Paula docks and thus gain access,
through the Ferrocarriles Unidos side line servicing
the Paula docks (Havana Central Railway), to
locations in the hinterland for the transportation of
cargo received for such destinations; by their very
nature, these modifications tend to perfect the works

463
granted and improve the conditions thereof; in addition, said petitionary company undertakes to build
or to provide, at its own expense, bonded storage
warehouses in order to avoid merchandise congestion
on its docks and warehouses.
Whereas: The proposed modifications entail a cost
increase for the Company of more than two million
pesos in excess of the exis ting budget for its works,
thereby imposing greater obligations upon them; and
the Company, as compensation for such expenses and
that part of the waterfront that would remain in
favor of the State, requests that the term for the
reversion of the works be extended to ninety-nine
years, in accordance with the original project, and
that it be granted the usufru ct for the term thereof of
the spaces between the str eets that were established
as public thoroughfares between jetties “A,” “B,” and
“C,” referred to in Arti cle 4 of Decree number 1022 of
November 11, 1910, which shall be intended for the
storage of merchandise that may remain outdoors.
Whereas: The proposed wo rks will undoubtedly
facilitate the operations merchandise handling operations, and will additionally result in greater available capacity at the aforesaid docks, thereby meeting
a significant need and affording the significant advantage of being able to tr ansport cargo intended for
the interior of the Republic without the current
lighterage charges, which advantages redound to the
benefit of the public service; and, taking into account
the present congested situation existing in the port of
Havana and the volume of commercial activity therein, it is necessary to provide for the improvement
thereof in every respect.
Whereas: The General Public Works Act does not
prohibit changes being made to projected works of

464
the nature of those granted  to the Company that
holds the concession and expressly authorizes them
in projected public works of the State and in those
that are granted to private parties with State subventions, the only difference with the works mentioned being the manner of compensation of the party
that executes them.
Whereas: Once the first part of the works referred
to in Decree 1022 of 1910 has been completed within
the required term and conditions, the Company that
holds the concession having noticed significant defects and omissions in them, it proposes to cure them
by improving said works and the public service they
are to provide and, instead of availing itself of the
deadlines set for it to continue with the works until
completion, it proposes to carry them out immediately, so that is fair and  convenient to the general
interests of the Port of Havana to agree to what has
been requested.
Now, therefore, availing my self of the powers bestowed upon me by the Constitution and all other
laws on the matter, and upon the proposal from
Secretary of Health and Welfare and Acting Secretary of Public Works,
I RESOLVE:
First. To agree to the modifications listed in the
request submitted by Port of Havana Dock Company,
previously referred to, to whic h effect it shall file, as
soon as possible, with the Department of Public
Works, plans of said works in greater detail and the
specifications thereof for approval and all other
purposes.
Second: To extend the term for the reversion of the
works to the State, referred to in the second condition

465
of Decree number 467 of November 29, 1905, to
ninety-nine years reckoned as of the date of the
concession.
Third: The concession-holding company is obligated
to disassemble and transport to such location in the
bay of Havana as the Department of Public Works
may indicate to it the devices and accessories that
make up the existing baggage disinfection plant at
the Machina.
Fourth: The concession-holding company shall
transport to and deliver at the location indicated to it
the Machina and its plant, once it has been disassembled by the Government, and undertakes to make
available to the Government  its floating derrick for
the purposes for which it used the Machina.
Fifth: The concession-holding company is obligated
to pave with granite cobblestones on a concrete base
and to maintain at its expense that part of the communication area all along the front of the area which
is to be occupied by the works it intends to build.
Sixth: The concession-holding company waives the
right to occupy the portion of the waterfront located
to the north of jetty “A,” its concession being bounded
in that direction by the part already built adjacent to
jetty “A,” so that the St ate will be able to freely
dispose of said portion of the waterfront.
Seventh: A single-track right of way shall be
established for trains in the communication area
outside the bounds of the concession, a double-track
being allowed within the bounds thereof; it being
clearly understood that in no event shall it be allowed
for railroad wagons to interrupt car and cart traffic
on the streets and public thoroughfares that afford
access to said jetties, and that cars and carts and all

466
other cargo and passenger vehicles shall have preferential right to the use of and traffic on said streets.
Eighth: The Company is granted the use, for the
term of the concession, of the spaces comprised
between the public streets and thoroughfares affording access to the jetties es tablished in Article 4 of
Decree 1022 cited above, always leaving free for
vehicular traffic the necessary space along the front
of the building on the edge [of the concession].
Ninth: The concession-holding company must commence the works within the shortest possible period
of time after the promulgation of the present Decree,
not to exceed three months, and complete them within a term of thirty months reckoned as of the same
date.
Tenth: The concession-holding company is obligated to comply with the conditions set forth in Decrees numbers 467 of Novem ber 29, 1905, and 1022 of
November 11, 1910, to the extent that they are not
contrary to or modified by the present Decree.
The Secretary of Public Works is charged with the
enforcement of the present Decree,
Given in the Presidential Palace, havana,
December 13, 1920.

Having seen the briefs from the Havana Docks Corporation dated June 27, 1928 and January 14, 1931
addressed to his excellency the Secretary of Public
Works announcing that it had acquired by cession
from the Port of Havana Docks Company the administrative concession latter had according to the Decrees of this Presidency  numbers 467 of November
29, 1905, 1022 of November 11, 1910, 184 .of March
13, 1911 and 1944 of December 13, 1920 for the construction of wharfs and wa rehouses in the Port of
Havana so that said cession be officially recognized in
favor of the Havana Docks Corporation.
Whereas: (Findings of Fact) The Havana Docks Corporation attaches to its request a first copy of the legal
instrument (deed) number 49 dated April 11, 1928,
given before Dr. Oscar A. Montero y Beldarrain,
Notary Public of Havana, which justifies, according to
a statement from the Legal Counsel Department of
the Ministry of Public Wo rks, the, transfer or sale
(buying and selling) contract of said administrative
concession and it has also been fully established that
the transfer of said concession was performed with all
its rights and actions in favor of the Havana Docks
Corporation, which due said attainment will substitute the Port of Havana Docks Company in, all of
its rights and actions as well in any obligations
thereof contracted by the latter.

474

Whereas: According to the file records of the Ministry
of Public Works due to the proceedings arraigned at
the Provincial Government of Havana by virtue of a
petition presented by Mr. Sylvester Scovel requesting
an administrative concession for the construction of a
wharf in the port of Havana, with mechanical installations, a building to serve as customs and other
works, this Presidency i ssued Decree number 85 of
February 27, 1905 declaring said proposed works to
be of public interest and to proceed with the auction
of the necessary concession for the execution of the
works.
Whereas: The auction havin g been effected for the
concession, this Presidency issued Decree No.467 of
November 29, 1905 granting to “Compañia del
Puerto” successor to Mr. Sy lvester Scovel, the necessary concession to carry out the works projected by
said gentleman in all that  was not modified by the
clauses as stated in said Decree.
Whereas: The execution of the works as projected
would have been detrimental to the public interest,
a change of project was advised and accepted by
“Compañia del Puerto” and thus this Presidency issued Decree number 1022 of November 11, 1910
according to which four w harfs, known as A, B, C,
and D must be constructed under certain conditions
instead of only one wharf.
Whereas: Decree number 184 of March 13, 1911, of
this Presidency recognized the transfer performed in
favor of the Port of Havana Docks Co. with all its
rights and obligations, of th e concession granted by
Presidential Decrees dated November 29, 1905 and
November 11, 1910.

475

Whereas: Decree number 1944 of December 13, 1920
of this Presidency, autho rized modifications among
which was to include as one unit of construction those
corresponding to wharfs C and D and the emplacement of wharf C and the period for escheat was
extended to 99 years, th e concessionaire company
being obligated to fulfill all the obligations contemplated by Decrees numbers 467 of November 21. 1905
and 1022 of November 11, 1910 in as much as they
are not opposed or modified by said Decree of
December 13, 1920.

requested should have been proceeded by final acceptance of the works performed by the Port of
Havana Docks Company which has been effected according to the minutes of September 1, 1933 taken by
the executive office of the Department of Public
Works of the District of Havana witnessed by a delegate of the Department of Finance and by the Vice-

approval ad the pertinent Department on October 21
of the same year and it is  Stated in said document
among other things that the Company is obligated to
construct or provide bonded  warehouses at any time
in which they are needed, in order to avoid conglomeration of merchandise in its docks or warehouses
and to fulfill its outstanding obligations with the
State with respect to str eet maintenance around the
third wharf known as Santa Clara as well as 41 the
paved portions between the tracks and fifty centimeters beyond them.

article 102 of the General Lai of Public Works in
force, the effected transfer is legal, Whereas: These
documents ‘have been duly processed in accordance

476

with the law, Following a request from the Secretary
of Public Works
I RESOLVE
To recognize the transfer performed by the Port of
Havana Docks Co. in favor of Havana Docks Corporation, of the concession of the docks, warehouses and
other works which were authorized in this Port to
the first of said entities  by the Decrees of this
Presidency numbers 467 of  November 29, 1905; 1022

concession and that the warranties covering its responsibilities remain effective.

seventh day of the month of September, nineteen
hundred and thirty four.

Whereas: The imperialistic interests whose representatives Govern in the United States of North America

agressiveness is the genera l embargo of exports from
